OASIS BBS — platform architecture walkthrough

Last updated: 18 August 2026 · Bahri · Behavior-Based Safety

This document explains what OASIS BBS is today, how the codebase is organized, and the architectural decisions behind each major area — from authentication and multi-tenant branding through observations, action items, dashboards, and analytics. Product rules that agents must follow live in AGENTS.md at the repo root; this report is the human-readable companion.

Executive summary. OASIS BBS (Powered by TailoredTech) is a data-intensive safety observation platform for Bahri. Observers (crew on vessels or office users) fill ICB checklists; the system denormalizes analytics on each observation, pre-aggregates monthly rollups in main_analytics, and serves dense logs, PDF/Excel exports, and configurable dashboards. The stack is Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, MongoDB via Mongoose 9, NextAuth v5, and env-switched adaptors for email and storage. Domain types are portable TypeScript; Mongoose stays behind repos so SQL can replace MongoDB later without rewriting features.

1. Product and branding

Customer: Bahri. Product name in UI: OASIS BBS (src/lib/brand.ts). Tagline: Behavior-Based Safety. Footer credit: Powered by TailoredTech (sign-in and sidebar).

The app is observation-centric. An observer is either a crew member signed on a vessel or an office member. Unsigned crew can still sign in and request sign-on to a vessel; only signed-on crew create observations. Office users can create observations for any vessel in the tenant and those rows are tagged createdByOffice: true for reporting.

Decision — volume first. Many observations will be created. Indexes, denormalized fields on each observation, and monthly pre-aggregation (main_analytics) exist so reads never rescan the full collection. Log tables page server-side; dashboard widgets read stored months, not live $facet over all observations on every page load.

2. AGENTS.md and the memory rule

AGENTS.md is the project's long-term memory for AI agents and developers. If anyone states a rule, convention, or product fact that should persist, it is added there immediately — not kept only in chat. Sections cover product, UI density, each domain (observations, action items, dashboards), domain models, architecture, error handling, stack notes, coding rules, and seed commands.

This HTML report is an explanatory walkthrough. When the product changes, update AGENTS.md first for operational rules, then refresh this document for narrative context.

3. Technology stack

Decision — no Mongoose in the browser or Edge. Client components must not import src/db, src/repo, or the full auth adaptor. Server components and server actions compute data; env-only auth flags live in src/lib/adapters/auth/auth-methods.ts.

4. Folder contract and request flow

src/features/<name>/
  components/   # feature UI
  hooks/        # feature client hooks
  actions/      # Next.js server actions → services
  utilities/    # feature helpers

src/components/ui/           # shadcn primitives only
src/components/ui/shared/    # reusable app UI (DatePicker, PageSheet, DistributionChart, …)
src/components/errors/         # StatusPage, RouteError, role-specific not-found/error

src/db/schemas/              # portable TypeScript domain types (string IDs)
src/db/models/               # Mongoose models only
src/db/seed/                 # seed scripts
src/repo/<model>/
  <model>.repo.ts           # DB access
  <model>.service.ts        # business rules

src/lib/adapters/            # auth, email, storage
src/lib/icb.ts               # ICB rollups, completion %, red-flag detection
src/app/                     # App Router routes and API routes
flowchart LR UI["Feature UI / hooks"] --> SA["Server actions / API routes"] SA --> SVC["repo/*.service"] SVC --> REPO["repo/*.repo"] REPO --> MODEL["db/models (mongoose)"] MODEL --> MONGO[(MongoDB)] SA --> AD["Adaptors"] AD --> AWS["SES / S3"] AD --> AZ["Graph / Blob"] AD --> AUTH["NextAuth JWT"] UI --> TQ["TanStack Query cache"]

Feature modules today:

  • auth — sign-in (password + OTP), session helpers
  • observations — form, logs, filters, analytics sheet, PDF/Excel
  • action-items — corrective actions, list, form, audit, PDF
  • dashboards — builder, widget registry, public share links
  • icb-checklists — admin checklist editor with drag-and-drop
  • notifications — Outlook-style inbox per user
  • sign-on — crew sign-on requests and vessel crew lists
  • admin — users, vessels, organizations, crew management UIs
  • file_upload — proxy upload to storage adaptor
  • profile — user profile actions

5. Domain model and tenancy

A tenant is the top-level customer (e.g. Bahri BSM in seed data). Tenants have many organizations (BSM, BDSM), optional branding for theming and future auth overrides, many vessel groups, and many vessels. Office members are assigned to vessel groups, not individual vessels — that group membership defines which vessels they can access for sign-on and reporting.

erDiagram TENANT ||--o{ ORGANIZATION : has TENANT ||--o| BRANDING : themes ORGANIZATION ||--o{ OFFICE_MEMBER : employs ORGANIZATION ||--o{ VESSEL : owns VESSEL_GROUP ||--o{ VESSEL : groups OFFICE_MEMBER }o--o{ VESSEL_GROUP : assigned USER ||--o| OFFICE_MEMBER : actor USER ||--o| CREW_MEMBER : actor USER ||--o| VESSEL : actor CREW_MEMBER }o--o| VESSEL : signed_on FORM ||--o{ OBSERVATION : checklist_snapshot OBSERVATION }o--|| VESSEL : scoped_to OBSERVATION ||--o{ OBSERVATION_AUDIT : history ACTION_ITEM }o--|| ORGANIZATION : scoped_to DASHBOARD }o--|| TENANT : owned_by MAIN_ANALYTICS }o--|| TENANT : monthly_blob

Identity and counters

Atomic sequences live in the counters collection:

  • obs:{tenantId} — tenant-wide observation sequence (1, 2, 3…)
  • obs:{tenantId}:{vesselId}:{year} — per-vessel calendar-year sequence for serial suffix
  • action:{tenantId} — action item sequence

Observation serial = {organizationShorthand}-{vesselNameToken}-{vesselYearSeq} (vessel name token strips spaces/punctuation). Action item serial = {organizationShorthand}-AI-{paddedSequence}.

Observation document (write-time rollups)

On every create/update, the service computes and stores — never derived on read:

  • Identity: serial, sequence, observedAt, task
  • Scope: vesselId, vesselGroupId, vesselName, organizationName, organizationShorthand, createdByOffice
  • Observer: observerRank, observer name fields
  • Rollups: safeCount, atRisk, atRiskCount, redFlag (legacy sif still read), riskCategories[], per-record analytics
  • Log helpers: icbCompletionPercent (0–100), hasAttachments, logAttachments[], searchText
  • Review: status (ready_for_review | reviewed), reviewerId, reviewerName

Rollup logic is centralized in src/lib/icb.ts (computeObservationRollups).

6. Authentication and sessions

NextAuth v5 with session.strategy = "jwt". Two credential providers today: credentials (email + password) and otp (email + 6-digit code). Both call the auth adaptor and produce the same session user shape.

Sign-in page: left panel is public/bahri/vlcc.png only (full h-svh, mobile-safe). Bahri logo on the right above the form. User toggles Password vs Email code.

sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant P as Sign-in page participant A as Server action participant AD as Auth adaptor participant E as Email adaptor participant N as NextAuth JWT U->>P: Choose password or OTP alt Password P->>A: credentialsSignInAction A->>AD: authenticatePassword AD->>N: same session user else Email OTP P->>A: requestLoginOtpAction A->>E: send code (SES or Graph) E-->>A: notification record always P->>A: otpSignInAction A->>AD: authenticateOtp AD->>N: same session user end N-->>U: /dashboard redirect by actorType

Session contract (future SSO must map into this):

id, email, name, actorType, actorId, tenantId, organizationId, roles, vesselId

Enabled methods: AUTH_PROVIDER / NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_PROVIDER (default credentials,otp). Tenant branding may override later. /dashboard redirects by actorType to /crew, /office, or /vessel. Unknown actors on a role layout redirect to /dashboard, not another role.

7. Adaptors (email, storage, auth)

flowchart TB subgraph email [Email adaptor] EP[EMAIL_PROVIDER] -->|aws| SES[AWS SES] EP -->|graph| Microsoft Graph end subgraph storage [Storage adaptor] SP[STORAGE_PROVIDER] -->|s3| S3[S3 + CloudFront] SP -->|azure| BLOB[Azure Blob] end subgraph auth [Auth adaptor] AP[AUTH_PROVIDER / tenant branding] --> PW[Password] AP --> OTP[OTP] AP -.-> MS[Microsoft SSO later] PW --> SESSION[Same JWT session] OTP --> SESSION MS -.-> SESSION end
  • Implementations copied from RA_Hosting where applicable (src/lib/email, src/lib/storage).
  • Every sendEmail persists a notification row first, then marks sent or failed.
  • Uploads: browser → POST /api/upload/proxy → adaptor uploadBuffer. Do not set Content-Type: multipart/form-data on the client.
  • Reads: GET /api/assets via buildSecureAssetUrl / src/lib/secure-asset.server.ts.
  • Features never call AWS/Azure SDKs directly.

8. UI system, density, and theming

Semantic color tokens (globals.css)

All brand colors are CSS variables — never hardcoded hex in components. Tenants override via branding.

TokenUsage
--primaryBahri navy (#003B71 family). Sidebar background, enabled barrier, safe series.
--destructiveBahri orange (#FF681D). Sidebar active item, difficult barrier, at-risk series.
--criticalSemantic red — non-enabled barrier, red flag, ICB completion out of range. Not the same as destructive.
--successPositive states (e.g. open action item badge).
--chart-1…5General chart palette (brand secondary blues/greens + primary + destructive).
--chart-barrier-*, --chart-safe, --chart-at-riskSemantic chart colors; map to primary/destructive/critical for consistency.
--avatar-1…8Pastel avatar backgrounds with matching foreground hues.

Density and shared components

  • Data-dense tables: compact padding, short rows, no hero sections on dashboards.
  • UserAvatar for every person; IconTooltipButton for icon-only controls.
  • MultiSelect, SearchSelect, DatePicker (date + time), PageSheet (inline split panel, not overlay).
  • AttachmentThumbRow for read-only attachment lists in tables; FileThumb in editable forms.
  • Page titles in the site header only — no duplicate title blocks in page bodies.
  • Management tables: 10 rows/page, expanding search bubble, skeleton tbody only on load.
  • Observation logs: custom 25-row server-paged table (not the management table pattern).

Navigation shells

Four role dashboards: /crew, /office, /vessel, and admin (same /office shell with extra admin routes). Sidebar is navy; active item and user footer use orange. Main content sits on navy wrapper with rounded-tl-2xl inverted corner.

9. Observations

Feature root: src/features/observations. Routes include /crew/observations, /office/observations, new/edit paths per role.

Form layout and metadata

  • Desktop: metadata left (narrow), ICB right (wide), independent scroll. Mobile: single column, full page scroll.
  • Required metadata (client validation): task observed, location, day, weather, time of day, temperature, light — marked with red asterisks; submit shows toast “Complete all required fields”.
  • Task observed: debounced typeahead from prior tasks for the vessel plus office-created tasks.
  • Crew: observation date is server “now” (not editable). Office: full date/time picker.
  • Office-only: area, department (from profile), vessel selector (all tenant vessels).
  • Weather icons per condition; “Other” reveals free-text input.

ICB panel

  • Categories as muted bars (no nested cards). Each behavior: Safe and At risk steppers.
  • Action icons (comments, attachments, action item) appear when Safe or At risk > 0. At risk 0→1 opens comment dialog immediately.
  • Comments: five fields — While, Was, Because, Solution, Try. At risk requires barrier + While + Was + Because (Solution/Try optional). Incomplete rows show red * with tooltip.
  • Red flag toggle with severity (Moderate / Severe / Fatal) and remarks. Replaces legacy SIF labeling in UI.
  • Barrier segmented control: Enabled (primary), Difficult (destructive/orange), Non-Enabled (critical red) + optional remarks.
  • Comment editor: Dialog on desktop, bottom Drawer on mobile (useIsMobile).
  • ICB completion bar in header (IcbCompletionIndicator): target band 35–60% (green); outside band is critical red. Stored as icbCompletionPercent on write.
  • Office/admin: reviewer stars + comments on whole form and per-ICB; saving reviewer input marks observation reviewed.

Observation logs

  • 25 rows/page, TanStack Query with prefetch N+1 and N+2. Sticky serial column.
  • Toolbar: search, date range, filters sheet (saved per-user chips), analytics sheet, Excel export.
  • Hover/right-click actions: Edit (office only), Printout (PDF), Audit log.
  • Excel: POST /api/observations/export with active filters — backend loads all matches, not current page.
  • Group-by columns, configurable column visibility, filters for red flag, ICB completion in/out of range, attachments, etc.

Observation analytics sheet

Right Sheet using the active log filter (not just the current page). Server: observationQuery.aggregateAnalytics with $match + $facet. Cache: 5m stale, 30m gc.

  • Summary stat cards with period-over-period trend labels.
  • Safe vs at risk over time — safe = primary, at risk = destructive.
  • Barriers — pie uses semantic barrier colors; daily composed chart for enabled/difficult/non-enabled.
  • Distribution pies (vessel, org, status, source, checklist): pie/list toggle per chart; list mode shows name + bar + count. No useless side legend.
  • Top tasks observed — horizontal bars with distinct colors and visible count axis.
  • Export: Excel (tables + chart images via html-to-image) or PDF (observation-analytics-pdf.tsx).
flowchart TB LOG["Observation logs UI"] --> FILTER["Active filter + date range"] FILTER --> AGG["aggregateAnalytics $facet"] AGG --> SHEET["Analytics sheet / PDF / Excel"] WRITE["Observation create/update"] --> ROLL["computeObservationRollups"] ROLL --> OBS[(observation document)] CRON["POST /api/cron/analytics"] --> MA[(main_analytics monthly)] OBS --> CRON

10. Action items

Feature: src/features/action-items. Corrective actions scoped to tenant + organization, optional vessel.

  • Fields: vessel, status (open/closed), target date, priority, areas, departments, summary, description, assignees (office + crew), exposures, hierarchy of control, severity, attachments.
  • List: 25 rows/page, inline status toggle, edit, PDF printout, audit log.
  • Crew may create; crew may edit only items they created.
  • Audit collection: action_item_audit_logs.

Note: linking action items from ICB rows in the observation form still shows “Feature not currently available” toast — action items exist as a standalone module.

11. ICB checklists (admin)

Admin-only: Administration → ICB Checklists. @dnd-kit drag-and-drop categories and behaviors.

  • One office default checklist; one default per vessel group (exclusive).
  • Empty vesselGroupIds = office-only checklist.
  • Crew load default for signed-on vessel’s group; office loads office default.
  • Checklist audit log — same dialog pattern as observations.

12. Dashboards and main_analytics

main_analytics (monthly blobs)

One document per tenant per calendar month (yearMonth = yyyy-MM). metrics is a typed MonthlyAnalyticsMetrics blob: summary, daily series, dimensional breakdowns (vessel, observer, barrier, weather, ratings, tasks, etc.).

Decision — incremental sync. POST /api/cron/analytics (Bearer or x-api-key = ANALYTICS_CRON_API_KEY) rebuilds only months affected since analytics_sync_state.lastSyncedAt. Dashboard page load never runs a live 12-month observation aggregation. Refresh button in UI calls analyticsService.syncTenant via server action.

Custom dashboards

  • Routes: /office/explore/dashboards, builder at …/new and …/[id]/edit, viewer at …/[id].
  • Public share: isPublic + publicId → /public/dashboards/[publicId].
  • Widgets: { id, type, x, y, w, h } on 12-column react-grid-layout grid.
  • Widget registry (widget-registry.ts): stats, daily charts, pies, barrier mixes, radar, oneliners, markdown, gallery.
  • Optional dashboard filter (vessel, organization, date range) applied to stored monthly data.
  • Share with office members; audit log in dashboard_audit_logs. One isMain dashboard per tenant (auto-created).

13. Chart colors and tenant branding

Centralized in src/features/dashboards/utilities/chart-colors.ts and globals.css.

ContextColors
General pie / distribution--chart-1…5 (brand secondary blue, midnight green, dark green, primary, destructive)
BarrierEnabled → primary; Difficult → destructive; Non-Enabled → critical
Safe vs at riskSafe → primary; At risk → destructive
Shared componentDistributionChart in src/components/ui/shared/distribution-chart.tsx — pie/list toggle
Decision — CSS variables only. When a tenant branding document overrides --primary, --destructive, --critical, or chart tokens, every chart and barrier control updates without code changes.

14. Notifications and sign-on

  • /notifications for every role — Outlook-style list + reading pane.
  • Every outbound email creates a notification linked to userId when the recipient is a user.
  • Crew sign-on requests: vessel login approves/rejects at /vessel/requests; office/admin with group access can sign crew on directly.
  • Crew “My Vessel” shows signed-on context.

15. Administration and roles

AreaWhoRoute
User ManagementAdmin only/office/users
Vessel ManagementAdmin only/office/vessels
Organization ManagementAdmin only/office/organizations
ICB ChecklistsAdmin only/office/checklists
Crew ManagementAll office members/office/crew
DashboardsOffice (admin builds)/office/explore/dashboards

Office members assigned to a vessel’s group can sign crew on/off for vessels in that group without a sign-on request.

16. Error handling

  • Shared components: src/components/errors/ — StatusPage, RouteError, not-found variants.
  • App root: not-found.tsx, error.tsx, global-error.tsx (self-contained inline styles — no globals.css).
  • Role shells keep sidebar: office|crew|vessel/{error,not-found}.tsx.
  • Server pages: notFound() for missing records; forbidden() / unauthorized() for auth errors. Use unstable_rethrow(error) — never catch redirect / notFound in try/catch.

17. Local development and seed data

  1. Copy .env.example to .env.local. Set DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING, AUTH_SECRET, and optional adaptor keys.
  2. pnpm install then pnpm dev
  3. Standard seed: pnpm seed (or POST /api/dev/seed in dev). Idempotent — reuses records, rotates passwords to local/seed-passwords.txt (gitignored).
  4. Intensive seed: pnpm seed:intensive — drops the entire database, rebuilds Bahri BSM with ~18 vessels, 5 checklists, 80+ crew, 9 office users, ~3k+ observations over a full year, rebuilds main_analytics. Use for dashboard/analytics testing.
  5. Sign in at /sign-in. Passwords are in local/seed-passwords.txt after seed.
  6. OTP requires a working email adaptor; password works with MongoDB + AUTH_SECRET only.
  7. Analytics cron locally: POST /api/cron/analytics with ANALYTICS_CRON_API_KEY.

Seed tenant: Bahri BSM. Organizations: Bahri Ship Management (BSM) and Bahri Dry Ship Management (BDSM). Vessel logins seeded for Yanbu, Jeddah, and Abha.

18. Intentionally unfinished or deferred

  • Microsoft SSO adaptor (session slot and auth adaptor structure exist).
  • Action item creation from ICB row in observation form (toast placeholder).
  • Custom per-vessel-group / office question builder on observations.
  • Service queue / bus and Redis.
  • SQL database migration (schemas and repos are structured for portability).
  • Reports section under Explore Data (/office/explore/reports) — route exists; scope TBD.
Document history. Originally written 14 Aug 2026 as “BBS foundation and auth.” Expanded 18 Aug 2026 to cover the full OASIS BBS platform: observations, ICB, red flag, analytics, dashboards, action items, chart theming, validation, and operational seed workflows. For day-to-day coding rules, always prefer AGENTS.md.

Markdown: Identity and counters
```
### Identity and counters
Atomic sequences live in the `counters` collection:
- `obs:{tenantId}` — tenant-wide observation sequence (1, 2, 3…)
- `obs:{tenantId}:{vesselId}:{year}` — per-vessel calendar-year sequence for serial suffix
- `action:{tenantId}` — action item sequence

Observation `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-{vesselNameToken}-{vesselYearSeq}` (vessel name token strips spaces/punctuation). Action item `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-AI-{paddedSequence}`.
```

Markdown: Observation document (write-time rollups):
```
### Observation document (write-time rollups)
On every create/update, the service computes and stores — never derived on read:

**Identity:** `serial`, `sequence`, `observedAt`, `task`
**Scope:** `vesselId`, `vesselGroupId`, `vesselName`, `organizationName`, `organizationShorthand`, `createdByOffice`
**Observer:** `observerRank`, observer name fields
**Rollups:** `safeCount`, `atRisk`, `atRiskCount`, `redFlag` (legacy `sif` still read), `riskCategories[]`, per-record `analytics`
**Log helpers:** `icbCompletionPercent` (0–100), `hasAttachments`, `logAttachments[]`, `searchText`
**Review:** `status` (`ready_for_review` | `reviewed`), `reviewerId`, `reviewerName`

Rollup logic is centralized in `src/lib/icb.ts` (`computeObservationRollups`).
```

```
- Categories as muted bars (no nested cards). Each behavior: Safe and At risk steppers.

- Comments: five fields — While, Was, Because, Solution, Try. At risk requires barrier + While + Was + Because (Solution/Try optional). Incomplete rows show red `*` with tooltip.
- **Red flag** toggle with severity (Moderate / Severe / Fatal) and remarks. Replaces legacy SIF labeling in UI.
- **Barrier** segmented control: Enabled (primary), Difficult (destructive/orange), Non-Enabled (critical red) + optional remarks.
- Comment editor: Dialog on desktop, bottom Drawer on mobile (`useIsMobile`).
- **ICB completion** bar in header (`IcbCompletionIndicator`): target band 35–60% (green); outside band is critical red. Stored as `icbCompletionPercent` on write.
- Office/admin: reviewer stars + comments on whole form and per-ICB; saving reviewer input marks observation reviewed.
```

```
1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`. Set `DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `AUTH_SECRET`, and optional adaptor keys.

5. Sign in at `/sign-in`. Passwords are in `local/seed-passwords.txt` after seed.
6. OTP requires a working email adaptor; password works with MongoDB + `AUTH_SECRET` only.
7. Analytics cron locally: `POST /api/cron/analytics` with `ANALYTICS_CRON_API_KEY`.

Seed tenant: **Bahri BSM**. Organizations: **Bahri Ship Management (BSM)** and **Bahri Dry Ship Management (BDSM)**. Vessel logins seeded for Yanbu, Jeddah, and Abha.
```

```
A **tenant** is the top-level customer (e.g. Bahri BSM in seed data). Tenants have many **organizations** (BSM, BDSM), optional **branding** for theming and future auth overrides, many **vessel groups**, and many **vessels**. Mermaid (erDiagram) exact source.
```

Markdown: Identity and counters
```
### Identity and counters
Atomic sequences live in the `counters` collection:
- `obs:{tenantId}` — tenant-wide observation sequence (1, 2, 3…)
- `obs:{tenantId}:{vesselId}:{year}` — per-vessel calendar-year sequence for serial suffix
- `action:{tenantId}` — action item sequence

Observation `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-{vesselNameToken}-{vesselYearSeq}` (vessel name token strips spaces/punctuation). Action item `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-AI-{paddedSequence}`.
```

Markdown: Observation document (write-time rollups):
```
### Observation document (write-time rollups)
On every create/update, the service computes and stores — never derived on read:

**Identity:** `serial`, `sequence`, `observedAt`, `task`
**Scope:** `vesselId`, `vesselGroupId`, `vesselName`, `organizationName`, `organizationShorthand`, `createdByOffice`
**Observer:** `observerRank`, observer name fields
**Rollups:** `safeCount`, `atRisk`, `atRiskCount`, `redFlag` (legacy `sif` still read), `riskCategories[]`, per-record `analytics`
**Log helpers:** `icbCompletionPercent` (0–100), `hasAttachments`, `logAttachments[]`, `searchText`
**Review:** `status` (`ready_for_review` | `reviewed`), `reviewerId`, `reviewerName`

Rollup logic is centralized in `src/lib/icb.ts` (`computeObservationRollups`).
```

```
A **tenant** is the top-level customer (e.g. Bahri BSM in seed data). Markdown: Identity and counters
```
```
### Identity and counters
Atomic sequences live in the `counters` collection:
- `obs:{tenantId}` — tenant-wide observation sequence (1, 2, 3…)
- `obs:{tenantId}:{vesselId}:{year}` — per-vessel calendar-year sequence for serial suffix
- `action:{tenantId}` — action item sequence

Observation `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-{vesselNameToken}-{vesselYearSeq}` (vessel name token strips spaces/punctuation). Action item `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-AI-{paddedSequence}`.
```

Markdown: Observation document (write-time rollups):
```
### Observation document (write-time rollups)
On every create/update, the service computes and stores — never derived on read:

**Identity:** `serial`, `sequence`, `observedAt`, `task`
**Scope:** `vesselId`, `vesselGroupId`, `vesselName`, `organizationName`, `organizationShorthand`, `createdByOffice`
**Observer:** `observerRank`, observer name fields
**Rollups:** `safeCount`, `atRisk`, `atRiskCount`, `redFlag` (legacy `sif` still read), `riskCategories[]`, per-record `analytics`
**Log helpers:** `icbCompletionPercent` (0–100), `hasAttachments`, `logAttachments[]`, `searchText`
**Review:** `status` (`ready_for_review` | `reviewed`), `reviewerId`, `reviewerName`

Rollup logic is centralized in `src/lib/icb.ts` (`computeObservationRollups`).
```

```
A **tenant** is the top-level customer (e.g. Bahri BSM in seed data). Mermaid (erDiagram) exact source.
```

Markdown: Identity and counters
```
### Identity and counters
Atomic sequences live in the `counters` collection:
- `obs:{tenantId}` — tenant-wide observation sequence (1, 2, 3…)
- `obs:{tenantId}:{vesselId}:{year}` — per-vessel calendar-year sequence for serial suffix
- `action:{tenantId}` — action item sequence

Observation `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-{vesselNameToken}-{vesselYearSeq}` (vessel name token strips spaces/punctuation). Action item `serial` = `{organizationShorthand}-AI-{paddedSequence}`.
```

Markdown: Observation document (write-time rollups):
```
### Observation document (write-time rollups)
On every create/update, the service computes and stores — never derived on read:

**Identity:** `serial`, `sequence`, `observedAt`, `task`
**Scope:** `vesselId`, `vesselGroupId`, `vesselName`, `organizationName`, `organizationShorthand`, `createdByOffice`
**Observer:** `observerRank`, observer name fields
**Rollups:** `safeCount`, `atRisk`, `atRiskCount`, `redFlag` (legacy `sif` still read), `riskCategories[]`, per-record `analytics`
**Log helpers:** `icbCompletionPercent` (0–100), `hasAttachments`, `logAttachments[]`, `searchText`
**Review:** `status` (`ready_for_review` | `reviewed`), `reviewerId`, `reviewerName`

Rollup logic is centralized in `src/lib/icb.ts` (`computeObservationRollups`).
```

note.name: OASIS BBS Platform Architecture
note.title: 1-8-2026 snapshot
note.description: OASIS BBS (Bahri — Behavior-Based Safety) platform architecture walkthrough: stack, domain model, auth, adaptors, observations, action items, dashboards, analytics, and seed workflows.

blocks.content:
**Customer:** Bahri · **Product name in UI:** OASIS BBS (`src/lib/brand.ts`) · **Tagline:** Behavior-Based Safety · **Footer credit:** Powered by TailoredTech (sign-in and sidebar).

The app is observation-centric. An **observer** is either a **crew member** signed on a vessel or an **office member**. Unsigned crew can still sign in and request sign-on to a vessel; only signed-on crew create observations. Office users can create observations for any vessel in the tenant, and those rows are tagged `createdByOffice: true` for reporting.

blocks.title: Decision — volume first
blocks.body: Many observations will be created. Indexes, denormalized fields on each observation, and monthly pre-aggregation (`main_analytics`) exist so reads never rescan the full collection. Log tables page server-side; dashboard widgets read stored months, not live `$facet` over all observations on every page load.

blocks.content: **Executive summary.** OASIS BBS (*Powered by TailoredTech*) is a data-intensive safety observation platform for Bahri. Observers (crew on vessels or office users) fill ICB checklists; the system denormalizes analytics on each observation, pre-aggregates monthly rollups in `main_analytics`, and serves dense logs, PDF/Excel exports, and configurable dashboards. The stack is Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, MongoDB via Mongoose 9, NextAuth v5, and env-switched adaptors for email and storage. Domain types are portable TypeScript; Mongoose stays behind repos so SQL can replace MongoDB later without rewriting features.

`AGENTS.md` is the project's long-term memory for AI agents and developers. If anyone states a rule, convention, or product fact that should persist, it is added there immediately — not kept only in chat. Sections cover product, UI density, each domain (observations, action items, dashboards), domain models, architecture, error handling, stack notes, coding rules, and seed commands.

This note is an explanatory walkthrough. When the product changes, update `AGENTS.md` first for operational rules, then refresh this document for narrative context.

cells.value: Primitives in `src/components/ui`; app shared UI in `src/components/ui/shared`
Portable schemas in `src/db/schemas`; models only in `src/db/models`
JWT session strategy; same session shape for all providers
Observation logs, analytics sheet, paginated lists
Layout/app state that would otherwise require deep prop drilling
Colors driven by CSS variables for multi-tenant branding
Observation printout, action item printout, analytics PDF
Log export and analytics workbook with embedded chart images
AWS SES + S3/CloudFront; Azure adaptors exist for later

blocks.title: Decision — no Mongoose in the browser or Edge
blocks.body: Client components must not import `src/db`, `src/repo`, or the full auth adaptor. Server components and server actions compute data; env-only auth flags live in `src/lib/adapters/auth/auth-methods.ts`.

```
src/lib/adapters/            # auth, email, storage
src/lib/icb.ts               # ICB rollups, completion %, red-flag detection
src/app/                     # App Router routes and API routes
```

Intro:
"Feature root: `src/features/observations`. Routes include `/crew/observations`, `/office/observations`, new/edit paths per role."

- Office-only: area, department (from profile), vessel selector (all tenant vessels).
- Weather icons per condition; "Other" reveals free-text input."

ICB panel:
"### ICB panel
- Categories as muted bars (no nested cards). Each behavior: Safe and At risk steppers.
- Action icons (comments, attachments, action item) appear when Safe or At risk > 0. At risk 0→1 opens comment dialog immediately.

- **Red flag** toggle with severity (Moderate / Severe / Fatal) and remarks. Replaces legacy SIF labeling in UI.
- **Barrier** segmented control: Enabled (primary), Difficult (destructive/orange), Non-Enabled (critical red) + optional remarks.
- Comment editor: Dialog on desktop, bottom Drawer on mobile (`useIsMobile`).
- **ICB completion** bar in header (`IcbCompletionIndicator`): target band 35–60% (green); outside band is critical red. Stored as `icbCompletionPercent` on write.
- Office/admin: reviewer stars + comments on whole form and per-ICB; saving reviewer input marks observation reviewed."

Observation logs:
"### Observation logs
- 25 rows/page, TanStack Query with prefetch N+1 and N+2. Sticky `serial` column.
- Toolbar: search, date range, filters sheet (saved per-user chips), analytics sheet, Excel export.
- Hover/right-click actions: Edit (office only), Printout (PDF), Audit log.
- Excel: `POST /api/observations/export` with active filters — backend loads all matches, not current page.
- Group-by columns, configurable column visibility, filters for red flag, ICB completion in/out of range, attachments, etc."

Analytics sheet:
"### Observation analytics sheet
Right `Sheet` using the **active log filter** (not just the current page). Server: `observationQuery.aggregateAnalytics` with `$match` + `$facet`. Cache: 5m stale, 30m gc.

- Summary stat cards with period-over-period trend labels.
- Safe vs at risk over time — safe = primary, at risk = destructive.
- Barriers — pie uses semantic barrier colors; daily composed chart for enabled/difficult/non-enabled.
- Distribution pies (vessel, org, status, source, checklist): pie/list toggle per chart; list mode shows name + bar + count. No useless side legend.
- Top tasks observed — horizontal bars with distinct colors and visible count axis.
- Export: Excel (tables + chart images via `html-to-image`) or PDF (`observation-analytics-pdf.tsx`)."

Analytics mermaid:
```
flowchart TB
  LOG["Observation logs UI"] --> FILTER["Active filter + date range"]
  FILTER --> AGG["aggregateAnalytics $facet"]
  AGG --> SHEET["Analytics sheet / PDF / Excel"]
  WRITE["Observation create/update"] --> ROLL["computeObservationRollups"]
  ROLL --> OBS[(observation document)]
  CRON["POST /api/cron/analytics"] --> MA[(main_analytics monthly)]
  OBS --> CRON
```
